title: Analytical root-zone demand state without shortage backlog
parallelism: Independent of pending DUMMY-11 qualification. DUMMY-12 does not consume DUMMY-11 equations or results; later three-store integration must require both authorities.
purpose: Replace the externally frozen SWAP-like request with a persistent analytical root-zone water-storage state and distinguish physical deficit from administrative shortage carryover.

window_contract.shortage: R-U; diagnostic only, not persistent state
window_contract.infeasible_loss: W_raw<0 => fail closed; water-stress/ET reduction physics is outside DUMMY-12

hypotheses: The request is a function of committed root-zone state only and does not change within the same coupling window.
With full supply and no other forcing, delivered irrigation exactly fills the committed deficit to W_target.
Atmospheric loss during the window can create a next-window request even when current shortage is zero.
Previous shortage is not a state variable: subsequent rainfall can reduce or eliminate the next request without repaying an administrative backlog.
When W_raw exceeds capacity, exact drainage removes only the excess and the root-zone balance closes.
For any feasible multi-window forcing sequence, cumulative storage change equals cumulative delivered irrigation plus rainfall minus atmospheric loss minus drainage.
Two histories with the same committed W have the same next request even if their prior shortage histories differ.
A physical loss larger than available root-zone water fails closed instead of silently creating negative storage or inventing stress-reduction physics.
interpretation_rules: shortage is a diagnostic difference between request and realized supply, not a conserved substance
root-zone deficit is physical state and can reflect prior shortage only through its effect on W
rainfall, loss and drainage are intentionally simple analytical bucket terms, not SWAP Richards physics
same-window demand feedback is excluded; request is frozen from committed start state
forbidden: no Richards-equation or production SWAP change
no capillary rise or groundwater interaction in DUMMY-12
no coupling to DUMMY-11 before both work units are separately qualified
